claims.quote: a heterozygous KCNA2 variant in a child with epilepsy.

claims.object_text: forms homotetrameric potassium channels and participate in heterotetrameric channel complexes, regulating neuronal excitability
claims.quote: KCNA2 encodes KV1.2 subunits, which form homotetrameric potassium channels and participate in heterotetrameric channel complexes with other KV1-family subunits, regulating neuronal excitability.
The mutation causes substitution F233S at the KV1.2 charge transfer center of the voltage-sensing domain.
KV1.2(F233S) subunits are trafficking deficient and reduce the surface expression of wild-type KV1.2 and KV1.4: a dominant-negative phenotype extending beyond KCNA2

claims.object_text: impairs trafficking along the biosynthesis and secretion pathway
claims.quote: both early and late events along the biosynthesis and secretion pathway impair trafficking.

claims.object_text: some KV1.2(F233S) trafficking was rescued by wild-type KV1.2 and KV1.4
claims.quote: Yet some KV1.2(F233S) trafficking was rescued by wild-type KV1.2 and KV1.4 subunits, likely in permissible heterotetrameric stoichiometries:

claims.object_text: up to one or two KV1.2(F233S) subunits can participate in trafficking-capable heterotetramers with wild-type KV1.2 or KV1.4
claims.quote: support that up to one or two KV1.2(F233S) subunits can participate in trafficking-capable heterotetramers with wild-type KV1.2 or KV1.4, respectively

claims.object_text: depolarizing shift of ∼48 mV on KV1.2 voltage dependence
claims.quote: F233S causes a depolarizing shift of ∼48 mV on KV1.2 voltage dependence.
it operates with modestly perturbed voltage dependence and retains pore coupling, evidenced by off-charge immobilization.
